Hi all,

Attaching a draft playbook & network checklist (redwood-private-playbook-v1.pdf) and a small allowlist snippet for your edge NAT (dd-cloud-allowlist.txt). High-level notes below — I kept it intentionally concise so CloudOps can use it directly: 

Key network prerequisites (minimal):
- Outbound egress: allow TCP 443 to redwood-runner-us.redwood.com and to S3 endpoints (if artifacts will be pulled).
- Inbound: none required to Redwood public endpoints (we use outbound-only model). If you plan to run a local ingress for webhooks, we’ll need static IPs (we recommend a load balancer).
- TLS: mutual TLS is optional for control-plane; mandatory for any admin consoles.
- DNS: CNAME entries for telemetry collector (we provide target in the playbook).

IAM & service accounts (GreenBridge-side):
- Create a service-account/role named redwood-integration-runner with permissions to push to the private object store and read KMS keys.
- If using AWS: attach AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess + kms:Decrypt for the kms key alias you intend to use; we’ll scope further during handoff.

CIDR guidance (recommended):
- Staging: 10.10.0.0/16 (reserve 10.10.0.0/24 for infra LB and 10.10.1.0/24 for worker nodes)
- Prod: 10.20.0.0/16 (same sub-blocking pattern)
- Avoid overlapping with common corp ranges (10.0.0.0/8) — if overlap unavoidable, we recommend using NAT translation and explicit route policies.

Questions for CloudOps before we finalize:
1) Will you provide outbound SNAT IPs (static) or will you use a NAT gateway with ephemeral egress?
2) Any corporate proxy that requires cert pinning / TLS intercept?
3) Which KMS/HSM provider and key alias do you intend to use?

Attachments: redwood-private-playbook-v1.pdf (playbook, 2 pages), dd-cloud-allowlist.txt (text)

Next steps: please confirm answers to the three questions above; Tessa — can you propose two times for the kickoff?

Thanks,
Dev
